text:
maya: Nightly eval alert — edge-qa prompt set fail rate jumped from ~1.2% to 9.6% on the quantized bring-up run. Samples look more stochastic/hallucinated, not a single-mode regression. top_p/top_k/temp in eval config appear unchanged. any ideas?

maya: Example bad gen (truncated): 
```
Q: What is the refund policy for subscription X?
A: Refunds are processed within 24 hours. If you cancel after the trial, you may still receive a prorated refund unless the admin denies. Please contact our finance team at refunds@example.com.
```
(we used to return the official policy text; now it's inventing contact details)

nightly-evals-bot: summary: edge-qa failure delta +8.4pp, avg perplexity +0.9, median length +12 tokens. Model variant: model-v3-4bit-int8-quant. Run id: nightly-2026-03-18-03.

omar: :eyes: can you paste the exact sampling config used by the job? also was this run on dedicated infra or private bring-up hardware?

maya: Config excerpt: 
```
model: model-v3-4bit-int8-quant
sampling: { temperature: 0.7, top_p: 0.95, top_k: 40, seed: null }
batching: per_request
rng_policy: reseed_each_batch: true
```
Infra: private bring-up box (gpu-07).

liam: reseed_each_batch: true jumps out. Wasn't that flag recently added to reduce cross-request cache correlation? If seed is null and we're reseeding with time(), that could change distribution behavior night-to-night. But still weird for a config that matched previous runs…

kai: small nuance: the quantized runner introduced an internal call to torch.manual_seed inside the attention kernel to work around a nondeterministic CUDA kernel. Previously it inherited the global RNG. A PR (runtime/#4123) changed that to call manual_seed(int(time())) when global seed is None. So two layers of reseeding might be interacting (serving layer + kernel), effectively double-randomizing.

maya: that could push sampling into different tails. any quick repro we can run?

liam: plan: 1) run the nightly eval job locally with seed fixed (seed=42) for both fp16 and 4-bit quant. 2) run with reseed_each_batch=false to mimic old behavior. 3) gather 100 samples from edge-qa and diff with last-good baseline.

nightly-evals-bot: queued adhoc job: repro-1813467935. Status: running (99 of 100).

omar: if fixed-seed stabilizes results we'll know it's RNG handling. also check if top_p/top_k implementations differ between quant and fp16 (sometimes we fast-path topk to a different C kernel).

nightly-evals-bot: repro-1813467935 results: seed-fixed (42) + quant: fail rate 1.3% (baseline ~1.2%). seed-random + quant: 9.2%. fp16-random: 1.4%.

maya: ok that pins it — quantized + random reseed = regression.

kai: root cause: runtime/#4123 and sampling wrapper both reseed when seed is null. Quick mitigation: remove internal kernel reseed so runner owns RNG lifecycle. Longer term: add explicit deterministic-mode flag and test matrix for quantized kernels.

liam: I'll open a revert/patch PR to stop kernel-level reseed and add a unit test that runs sampling 50x and checks distribution stability when seed=null vs seed=fixed. assigning to @omar to validate with canary.

omar: got it. I'll run a canary on gpu-07 tonight with the patch and set reseed_each_batch=false by default for nightly for a week.

maya: thanks all — adding follow-up: add a quick note to onboarding checklist for quantized bring-up to verify RNG propagation. :thumbsup:

liam: ETA for patch PR: ~2h. will reference runtime/#4123 and link the eval diffs.

maya: great — marking this thread closed once the canary completes and metrics look good.
